name: Koninklijke Philips N.V.
reason: Adjusted EPS only EUR 1.13 (2015) to 1.56 (2025) (3.3% CAGR, -3.2% over 5y) with revenue -3.0%/yr after portfolio shrinkage, 10y avg ROIC 2.7% and the Respironics recall/litigation still weighing; no durable >=7% route.

name: Konecranes Oyj
reason: Strong run (adjusted EPS EUR 0.32 to 1.73, 18.5% CAGR) but this is a capital-goods cyclical with EPS at its 10y max and EBIT margin 13.2% at the 100th pctile vs an 8.5% average; consensus FY1 is just +0.8%, so the near-peak rule applies.

name: Wise Group plc
reason: High-quality cross-border payments franchise, but GAAP EPS jumped from GBP 0.13 (2022) to 0.42 (2023) largely on interest earned on customer balances (EBIT margin 16% to 31%), so earnings depend on the rate cycle and deliberate take-rate cuts, with only a short public record.

name: Telia Company AB
reason: Mature Nordic/Baltic telco with adjusted EPS falling from SEK 2.51 (2015) to 1.29 (2025) (-6.4% CAGR), revenue -0.7%/yr, 10y avg ROIC 1.3% and a 507% adj-vs-GAAP gap; partly Swedish-state owned and no >=7% growth route.

name: Inwido AB
reason: Housing/renovation-cyclical window maker whose adjusted EPS peaked at SEK 13.93 in 2022 and fell to 9.66 in 2025 (0.69x max, 3.3% 10y CAGR) with ordinary 8.6% avg ROIC; cheap but not special.

name: S.P.E.E.H. Hidroelectrica S.A.
reason: Romanian state-controlled hydro generator whose EPS (RON 14.17 in 2023 to 7.49 in 2025) and margin (63% peak to 39%) are set by power prices, hydrology and government price caps; consensus LTG 3%.

name: Titan S.A.
reason: Cement producer with EPS EUR 1.62 (2016) to 0.02 (2020) to 3.15 (2025), EBIT margin 15.9% at its 10y high vs an 11.0% average and 10y avg ROIC 5.7%; cyclical, commodity-like building materials near peak margins.

name: ACS, Actividades de Construccion y Servicios SA
reason: Leveraged construction/concessions holding with a 2.9% EBIT margin, 10y avg ROIC 5.0%, acquisitions 0.77x FCF (Hochtief/Abertis-style deals) and EPS EUR 2.19 to 3.69 (5.3% CAGR) distorted by a 2021 disposal gain; low-margin contracting is not forecastable or special.

name: Sweco AB
reason: Best-in-class Nordic engineering consultancy (adjusted EPS SEK 1.97 to 6.16, 12.1% CAGR, worst year -5.2%, ROIC 13.3%) but growth is partly acquisitive (shares +1.7%/yr), margin 10.4% is at its 10y high and it carries the same AI threat to labour-based billing as Arcadis/AFRY.

name: EDP S.A.
reason: Integrated utility with adjusted EPS EUR 0.23 (2015) to 0.31 (2025) (2.9% CAGR, 2/10 years >=7%), net debt 4.0x EBITDA, negative 10y FCF conversion and earnings tied to power prices and renewables policy; regulated, low-growth economics.

name: Interpump Group S.p.A.
reason: Good niche hydraulics/pumps compounder (adjusted EPS EUR 0.81 to 1.95, 9.2% CAGR, ROIC 12%) but EPS fell 24% from the 2023 peak of 2.56 as truck/construction hydraulics demand turned, showing cyclicality and a serial bolt-on acquisition model that make 5-10y EPS hard to pin down.

name: MITIE Group PLC
reason: Low-margin UK facilities outsourcer (EBIT margin 3.6%, 10y avg ROIC 5.7%) with adjusted EPS flat at GBP 0.13 vs 2015, shares +6.8%/yr from the Interserve deal and a 94.5% adj-vs-GAAP gap; cheap but ordinary.

name: Berkeley Group Holdings plc
reason: London housebuilder whose adjusted EPS fell from GBP 5.69 (2017) to 3.31 (2025) with EBIT margin at the 9th pctile and consensus FY1 -14.4%; earnings set by the housing and rate cycle (US homebuilder precedent).

name: Glanbia Plc
reason: Optimum Nutrition brand gives some specialness, but adjusted EPS grew only USD 0.86 to 1.35 (4.6% CAGR) with whey input-cost swings (EBIT margin 10.4% to 8.9% in 2025), acquisitions 0.49x FCF and a 60% adj-vs-GAAP gap, so the >=7% route is not reliably forecastable.

name: Vitec Software Group AB
reason: Sticky vertical-market software with adjusted EPS SEK 2.80 to 10.95 (14.6% CAGR) but growth is acquisition-driven (acquisitions 2.28x 10y FCF, shares +3.0%/yr, net debt 2.3x EBITDA), so organic EPS growth cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: Orange Polska SA
reason: Orange-controlled Polish telco with EBIT margin 4.2%, 10y avg ROIC 1.6%, revenue +1.0%/yr and adjusted EPS that was negative/near zero in 2016-20 before recovering to PLN 0.59; mature, competitive market with no special economics.

name: TAG Immobilien AG
reason: Leveraged German residential landlord (net debt 10.3x EBITDA, shares +4.1%/yr) with FFO per share falling from EUR 1.19 (2022) to 1.00 (2025) and growth driven by rates, rent regulation and property values; fails growth and balance-sheet tests.

name: Mowi ASA
reason: Salmon farmer whose EPS (EUR 1.42 in 2022 to 0.92 in 2025, worst year -59%) and EBIT margin (29.4% peak to 10.9%) are set by salmon spot prices, biology and Norwegian resource-rent tax; commodity earnings.

name: TE Connectivity plc
reason: Global connector/sensor oligopolist (with Amphenol) with adjusted EPS USD 3.60 to 8.76 (9.3% CAGR, 7/10 years >=7%, worst year -23% in 2020), 13.7% avg ROIC, net debt 1.2x and shares -3.1%/yr; margin 19.3% is at its 10y high but only modest drift above the 17.0% average (AWI precedent), with auto content-per-vehicle and AI data-centre secular drivers; auto-cycle exposure is the deep-dive test.

name: Ferretti S.p.A.
reason: Luxury yacht builder with GAAP EPS EUR 0.17 (2018) to 0.27 (2025) at a 100th-pctile 8.1% EBIT margin, weak 0.13x FCF conversion, consensus FY1 -13.2% and a contested Weichai/KKCG control situation; discretionary cyclical near peak.
